mainTopic: When a second document cancels the first; when the כתובה's lien begins; and the punishment of a betrothed נערה from a convert family
overview: The amud opens by finishing an explanation from the discussion just before it: the wife cannot collect the extra amount of a second כתובה from the earlier date, because he never wrote 'I added to your first כתובה,' so she gave up her first lien. The גמרא then asks whether רב הונא's ruling, that she may collect with either כתובה, argues with רב נחמן's rule that a second document cancels the first. It answers with רב פפא: רב נחמן agrees that if the second document adds anything, even a palm tree, it is an addition. Next the גמרא studies רב נחמן's rule directly. A sale followed by a gift, or a gift followed by a sale, does not cancel the first document, because the second was written for protection. The rule applies only when both documents are the same type. רפרם and רב אחא give two different reasons for the rule, and the גמרא lists the practical differences: the witnesses' trust, paying for produce, and the land tax. The גמרא then rules that the lien for the whole כתובה, both the basic sum and the תוספת, starts only from נישואין. Finally a new משנה teaches how a betrothed נערה who sinned is punished when she or her mother converted, and that the father's doorway is only the preferred place for the סקילה.

steps.title: Why she cannot collect the extra amount from the earlier date
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that she cannot collect the added amount from the earlier date because the second כתובה never said 'I added 100 to your 200.' By accepting it, she gave up the first lien.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, the reason she does not collect is that he did not write to her, 'I added one hundred to the two hundred for you.' So she must have given up her first lien.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an explanation from the discussion just before this. It explains why, in that case, the wife cannot collect the extra money based on the earlier date.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key is the wording of the second כתובה. If he had written 'I am adding to your first כתובה,' both documents would work together. Since he wrote a new, separate document, we assume she accepted it in place of the first. She therefore gave up the first document's lien and its earlier date.

keyTerms.meaning: she fully forgave / gave it up

phrases.english: Here too, this is the reason
that she does not collect
phrases.notes: He means the extra amount in the second כתובה, collected from the first document's earlier date.

phrases.english: since he did not write to her
"I added for you one hundred on top of the two hundred"
she has completely given up
the first lien.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּלָא גָּבְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion that came just before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the wording of the document
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think the second כתובה simply adds to the first, keeping the first date for the whole amount.
steps.terutzMaskana: Without 'I added' wording, the second document replaces the first, and she gave up the first lien.

steps.title: Does רב הונא disagree with רב נחמן?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא said she may collect with whichever כתובה she chooses. The גמרא asks whether this clashes with רב נחמן's rule that a second document cancels the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: if she wants, she collects with this one, and if she wants, she collects with that one. Shall we say this argues with רב נחמן? For רב נחמן said: two documents that come out one after the other, the second cancels the first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רב הונא's ruling that the wife can choose either כתובה. It then challenges it with רב נחמן's rule about two documents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a second document always cancels the first, the first כתובה should no longer exist. Then she could not choose it. So רב הונא's 'she can choose' seems to go against רב נחמן.
steps.confusionAlert: Though it is worded as a question ('shall we say'), this is a challenge. The גמרא is pointing out a possible contradiction between two אמוראים.

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: The Master here is רב הונא.

phrases.english: if she wants, she collects with this one,
if she wants, she collects with that one.
Shall we say this argues with רב נחמן?
For רב נחמן said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי שְׁטָרוֹת הַיּוֹצְאִין בְּזֶה אַחַר זֶה
phrases.english: two documents that come out one after the other
the second cancels the first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining one case to a broader conflict between רב הונא and רב נחמן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that she may collect with either כתובה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רב נחמן, the second document cancels the first, so the first כתובה should be worthless and she should have no choice.

steps.title: רב נחמן agrees when something was added
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with רב פפא: רב נחמן agrees that if the second document adds even a palm tree, it is an addition and does not cancel the first. Here the second כתובה added money, so there is no argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wasn't it said about this: רב פפא said, רב נחמן agrees that if he added a palm tree in it, he wrote it as an addition. Here too, he added something for her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא removes the contradiction. It shows that רב נחמן's rule does not apply when the second document adds something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's rule covers a second document that only repeats the first. If the second document adds anything, even one palm tree, it shows that it was written to add to the first, not replace it. The second כתובה had a larger amount, so both documents stand, and רב הונא fits with רב נחמן.
steps.whatToRemember: A second document cancels the first only if it adds nothing new. If it adds anything at all, it is treated as an addition, and the first document stays valid.

phrases.english: Wasn't it said about it,
רב פפא said:
and רב נחמן agrees
that if he added a palm tree in it,
he wrote it as an addition.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי, הָא אוֹסֵיף לַהּ מִידֵּי!
phrases.english: Here too, he added something for her!

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו מִי אִיתְּמַר עֲלַהּ אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the previous step.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the other ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן's rule cancels every first document, so רב הונא disagrees with him.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב נחמן's rule does not apply when the second document adds something, so there is no disagreement.

steps.title: Restating רב נחמן's rule for direct study
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now turns to רב נחמן's rule itself: two documents that come out one after the other, the second cancels the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: רב נחמן said, two documents that come out one after the other, the second cancels the first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion that focuses directly on רב נחמן's rule. Here it quotes the rule again to set up that discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, רב נחמן's rule came up only to test רב הונא. With 'גופא,' the גמרא makes the rule the main topic, so it can examine exactly which cases it covers.

keyTerms.meaning: the matter itself: introduces a closer look at a statement quoted earlier
that come out one after the other

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a needless repeat. The גמרא quotes the rule again on purpose because it is starting a new discussion about the rule itself.

phrases.english: The matter itself.
רב נחמן said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי שְׁטָרוֹת הַיּוֹצְאִין בְּזֶה אַחַר זֶה
phrases.english: two documents that come out one after the other
the second cancels the first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up רב נחמן's rule, which was quoted in step 2, as a topic of its own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When two documents about the same matter come out one after the other, the second cancels the first.

steps.title: Restating רב פפא's limit on the rule
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא's comment is quoted again: רב נחמן agrees that if the second document added a palm tree, it was written as an addition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: and רב נחמן agrees that if he added a palm tree in it, he wrote it as an addition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רב פפא's limit on רב נחמן's rule. This finishes setting up the rule before it begins to examine specific cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the rule and its limit side by side, the full picture is clear. A second document that only repeats the first replaces it. A second document that adds something sits on top of it.

phrases.english: רב פפא said:
and רב נחמן agrees
that if he added a palm tree in it,
he wrote it as an addition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא וּמוֹדֶה רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds רב פפא's limit to the rule quoted in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the second document adds anything, it is an addition and does not cancel the first.

steps.title: Obvious case: a sale document followed by a gift document
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says it is obvious that if the first document was a sale and the second a gift, the second does not cancel the first. It was written to protect the buyer from the bordering neighbor's rights.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious: if the first was written as a sale and the second as a gift, he wrote it to strengthen the buyer's position, because of the law of the bordering neighbor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins applying רב נחמן's rule to specific cases. It starts with a case that is obvious, which sets up the harder cases it will look at next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a second document replaces the first. But a gift document written after a sale has a clear purpose of its own: it protects the buyer from the neighbor who borders the field. So it is not meant to cancel the sale, and the first document stays in force.

keyTerms.meaning: the neighbor whose field borders this field

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רב נחמן's rule depends on why the second document was written. When it has a separate, sensible purpose, it does not cancel the first.

phrases.english: It is obvious:
if the first was a sale and the second a gift,
it was to strengthen his position that he wrote it for him,
because of the law of the bordering neighbor.
phrases.notes: A bordering neighbor gets first rights to buy a field that is sold, but not a field given as a gift.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts testing the rule from steps 4–5 on a specific type of case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A gift document written after a sale document does not cancel the sale. It was written to protect the buyer from the bordering neighbor.

steps.title: All the more so: first a gift, then a sale
steps.stepSummary: If the first שטר was a gift and the second a sale, the second surely does not cancel the first. It was written to protect the receiver from the giver's בעל חוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all the more so if the first was a gift and the second a sale, because we say he wrote it that way only because of the law of a creditor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the list of obvious cases where the second שטר does not cancel the first. This time the first was a gift and the second was a sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gift שטר gives the receiver no way to get his money back if the giver's בעל חוב takes the field. A sale שטר does give him that right. So the second שטר was clearly written to add protection, not to cancel the first, and this case is even clearer than the one in the previous step.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so (a stronger case)
A creditor, someone the giver owes money to

phrases.english: And all the more so if the first was as a gift
and the second as a sale,
for we say that because of the law of a creditor
phrases.notes: The giver's creditor could take the field away. A sale document lets the receiver collect his loss back from the giver.

phrases.english: that he wrote it this way.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן רִאשׁוֹן בְּמַתָּנָה וְשֵׁנִי בְּמֶכֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends step 6 with a stronger version of the same exception.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First gift, second sale: the second שטר adds protection against a בעל חוב and does not cancel the first.

steps.title: When the rule really applies: both sale or both gift
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן's rule applies only when both documents are the same type, both sale or both gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if both are sales or both are gifts, the second cancels the first.
steps.whatsHappening: After setting aside the cases with an addition or a change of document type, the גמרא states exactly where רב נחמן's rule applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the second שטר adds nothing and is the same kind as the first, there is no protective reason to write it. In that case it is treated as replacing the first, so the second cancels the first.
steps.whatToRemember: The second שטר cancels the first only when both are the same type and the second adds nothing.

phrases.english: Rather, if both of them are of sale
or both of them are of gift
the second cancels the first.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי שְׁנֵיהֶם בְּמֶכֶר שְׁנֵיהֶם בְּמַתָּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up steps 5-7 by stating the case left over for רב נחמן's rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב נחמן's rule applies only when both documents are sales or both are gifts.

steps.title: Why does the second document cancel the first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב נחמן's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why a second identical שטר cancels the first. This question sets up the next step, where two answers are given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing in the second שטר says it cancels the first, so the גמרא wants to know what we assume happened between the buyer and seller.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the rule defined in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The logic of why a second identical שטר cancels the first.

steps.title: רפרם: he admitted. רב אחא: he gave up his lien.
steps.stepSummary: רפרם says the receiver admitted the first שטר was no good. רב אחא says the receiver gave up his שעבוד from the first date.
steps.simpleTranslation: רפרם said: Say that he admitted to him. רב אחא said: Say that he gave up his lien.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים explain why the second שטר cancels the first. רפרם says the first שטר was admitted to be invalid. רב אחא says the receiver gave up his rights from the earlier date.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רפרם, the receiver admitted the first שטר was not valid (for example, forged), so it never counted. For רב אחא, the first שטר was fine, but the receiver agreed that his lien would start only from the date of the second שטר.

keyTerms.meaning: He admitted to him (that the first document was invalid)
A lien, the right to collect from the seller's property

steps.confusionAlert: רב אחא does not say the first שטר was fake. He agrees it was valid; only the lien date moves to the second שטר.

phrases.english: Rafram said:
Say that he admitted to him.
phrases.notes: The receiver admitted that the first document was not valid, so a new one was written.

phrases.english: Rav Acha said:
Say that he forgave him his lien.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַפְרָם אָמַר: אֵימַר אוֹדוֹיֵי אוֹדִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רפרם: the first שטר was admitted to be invalid. רב אחא: the receiver gave up his lien from the first date.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two explanations?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between רפרם and רב אחא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the two explanations ever lead to different results. This sets up the list in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that the second שטר cancels the first, so the גמרא wants to find a case where the reasons lead to different outcomes.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical difference between the two answers in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Practical outcomes that differ between רפרם and רב אחא.

steps.title: Three differences: witnesses, produce, and land tax
steps.stepSummary: The difference shows up in three things: whether the witnesses lose trust, whether the receiver pays for פירות eaten between the dates, and who pays the טסקא.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them: weakening the witnesses, paying for produce, and the land tax.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists three practical results that depend on which explanation is right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רפרם the first שטר was invalid, so its עדים look suspect, the receiver did not own the field until the second date and must pay for the פירות, and the old owner pays the טסקא for that time. For רב אחא the first שטר was good, so the עדים are fine and ownership started at the first date.
steps.whatToRemember: רפרם treats the first שטר as invalid, and רב אחא treats it as valid with the lien given up. That affects the witnesses, the produce, and the land tax.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them:
weakening the witnesses.
phrases.notes: If the first document was invalid, the witnesses who signed it become doubtful in other cases too.

phrases.english: And paying for produce
phrases.notes: This is the produce the receiver ate between the date of the first document and the date of the second.

phrases.english: and the land tax.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 by listing practical differences.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two explanations differ on the witnesses' trust, payment for produce between the dates, and responsibility for the land tax.

steps.title: What is the final ruling about the כתובה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the earlier question of when the כתובה's lien begins and asks what the final ruling is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was finally decided about the כתובה?
steps.whatsHappening: After a long side discussion about documents, the גמרא goes back to its original question about the כתובה. It is setting up the next step, which will bring the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The open question is when the husband's property becomes tied up to pay the כתובה: from the time of אירוסין or only from נישואין. The גמרא now wants a clear bottom line on this.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the conclusion about it?
The marriage contract that guarantees the wife's payment
A lien, meaning property tied up to guarantee a debt

phrases.english: What is the conclusion regarding the marriage contract?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the earlier question: does the כתובה's lien start from אירוסין or from נישואין?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about documents (steps 8-12) and returns to the main כתובה question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The final ruling on whether the כתובה's lien starts from אירוסין or from נישואין.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון splits the כתובה into two parts
steps.stepSummary: The basic sum of the כתובה is secured from אירוסין, while the extra amount is secured only from נישואין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל, quoting רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: the basic מנה or מאתים is secured from the time of אירוסין, and the תוספת is secured from the time of נישואין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a teaching from רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. He splits the כתובה into two parts with two different starting dates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic sum is fixed by the חכמים, so its lien starts already at אירוסין. The תוספת is the extra amount the husband adds on his own, and its lien starts only at נישואין.

keyTerms.meaning: The basic כתובה sum: 100 or 200 זוז
The extra amount a husband adds on his own to the כתובה
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage

phrases.english: Come and hear,
as Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said
in the name of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon:
The one hundred or two hundred are from the betrothal,
phrases.notes: A widow's basic כתובה is a מנה (100 זוז) and a virgin's is מאתים (200 זוז).

phrases.english: and the additional sum is from the marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question of step 13 by quoting a ברייתא-style dispute.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, the basic sum's lien starts at אירוסין and the תוספת's lien starts at נישואין.

steps.title: חכמים say both parts start from נישואין
steps.stepSummary: חכמים disagree and hold that both the basic sum and the תוספת are secured only from נישואין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: both this and that are from the time of נישואין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the opposing opinion of חכמים in the same dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים do not split the כתובה. In their view the husband's property is not tied up for any part of the כתובה until נישואין.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this and that, meaning the basic sum and the תוספת

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה מִן הַנִּישּׂוּאִין.
phrases.english: Both this and that are from the marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing side of the dispute begun in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both the basic sum and the תוספת of the כתובה are secured only from נישואין.

steps.title: The הלכה follows חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that both parts of the כתובה are secured from נישואין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: both this and that are from the time of נישואין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling and closes the כתובה discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה goes with the majority view of חכמים. So the whole כתובה, basic sum and תוספת together, is secured only from the date of נישואין.
steps.whatToRemember: Final הלכה: the husband's property is tied up for the entire כתובה, basic sum and תוספת, only from נישואין, as חכמים say.

phrases.english: And the halakha is:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה מִן הַנִּישּׂוּאִין.
phrases.english: Both this and that are from the marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute between steps 14 and 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The lien for both the basic כתובה and the תוספת begins only at נישואין.

steps.title: A girl who converted with her mother and then sinned
steps.stepSummary: A girl who converted together with her mother and then sinned while betrothed gets חנק, not stoning. The rules of the father's doorway and the 100 סלע do not apply to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A convert whose daughter converted with her, and the daughter sinned (as a betrothed נערה): she is punished by חנק. She has neither the rule of the father's doorway nor the 100 סלע.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It starts with a girl who became Jewish together with her mother, and it explains how the rules of a betrothed נערה who sinned apply to her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A born-Jewish betrothed נערה who sins gets סקילה at her father's door. If her husband falsely accuses her, he pays 100 סלע. Since this girl was not born Jewish, she gets the ordinary punishment for a married woman, חנק, and neither special rule applies to her.

keyTerms.meaning: The entrance of the father's house, where a born-Jewish betrothed נערה is stoned
The 100 סלע fine a husband pays for falsely accusing his wife

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse the two cases. Here the daughter herself converted, so she was not Jewish at conception or at birth. The next case is about a girl who was born after her mother converted.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A female convert whose daughter converted with her
and she committed adultery —
she is executed by strangulation;

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לָהּ לֹא פֶּתַח בֵּית הָאָב,
phrases.english: she has neither the entrance of the father's house,
nor one hundred sela.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה on a new topic after the כתובה discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A daughter who converted with her mother and sinned as a betrothed נערה gets חנק, without the father's doorway rule and without the 100 סלע.

steps.title: Conceived before conversion, born after
steps.stepSummary: If the girl was conceived before her mother converted but born after, she gets סקילה. Still, the father's doorway rule and the 100 סלע do not apply to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she was conceived not in holiness but born in holiness, she is punished by סקילה. But she has neither the father's doorway rule nor the 100 סלע.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a middle case: the mother converted while pregnant, so the girl was born Jewish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being born Jewish is enough to bring her up to the full punishment of סקילה. But the special rules of the father's doorway and the 100 סלע still need conception as a Jew as well, so they do not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: In holiness, meaning after the mother became Jewish

phrases.english: If her conception was not in sanctity
phrases.notes: Meaning she was conceived while her mother was not yet Jewish.

phrases.english: and her birth was in sanctity —
she is executed by stoning,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין לָהּ לֹא פֶּתַח בֵּית הָאָב,
phrases.english: but she has neither the entrance of the father's house,
nor one hundred sela.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיְתָה הוֹרָתָהּ שֶׁלֹּא בִּקְדוּשָּׁה וְלֵידָתָהּ בִּקְדוּשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a middle case to the case in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A girl conceived before her mother's conversion but born after it gets סקילה, but without the father's doorway rule and without the 100 סלע.

steps.title: Conceived and born after conversion: a full בת ישראל
steps.stepSummary: A girl conceived and born after her mother converted is treated exactly like any born-Jewish girl.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she was both conceived and born in holiness, she is like a בת ישראל in all matters.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list with the last case: a girl who was completely Jewish from conception on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since both conception and birth happened after the conversion, nothing holds her back. She gets סקילה at her father's door, and her husband pays the 100 סלע if he falsely accuses her.

keyTerms.meaning: In all her matters, meaning every rule applies

steps.whatToRemember: Three levels: converted with her mother means חנק. Conceived before and born after the conversion means סקילה, but no doorway rule and no 100 סלע. Conceived and born after the conversion means a full בת ישראל.

phrases.english: If her conception and birth were in sanctity,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי הִיא כְּבַת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְכׇל דְּבָרֶיהָ.
phrases.english: she is like a Jewish woman in all her matters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the three cases of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A girl conceived and born after her mother's conversion follows every rule of a born-Jewish girl.

steps.title: No father's doorway still means stoning
steps.stepSummary: If a betrothed נערה who sinned has a father but no father's house, or a father's house but no father, she is still stoned. The פתח בית אב rule is only a מצוה, not a requirement.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she has a father but no doorway of her father's house, or she has a doorway of her father's house but no father, she is still stoned. The 'father's doorway' was said only as a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues. It rules that a betrothed נערה who sinned still gets סקילה even when stoning her at her father's doorway is impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says she should be stoned at the doorway of her father's house. One might think that without that doorway there can be no סקילה at all. The משנה says no: the doorway is the ideal way to carry out the punishment, but missing it does not cancel the stoning.

keyTerms.meaning: The doorway of the father's house, where the תורה says she is stoned
Stoning, the death penalty given to a betrothed נערה who sinned
As the preferred way to do it, but not something that holds back the law

steps.whatToRemember: The father's doorway is the ideal place for the סקילה, but it is not required. Without it, she is still stoned.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with Steps 17–18. There the doorway rule did not apply because of the girl's convert status. Here she is a regular Jewish girl, and only the doorway itself is missing.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches the difference between a detail that is a מצוה (the best way) and one that is required for the law to work at all.

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לָהּ אָב וְאֵין לָהּ פֶּתַח בֵּית הָאָב,
phrases.english: She has a father but does not have an entrance to her father's house,
phrases.notes: He means her father doesn't own a house of his own.

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לָהּ פֶּתַח בֵּית הָאָב וְאֵין לָהּ אָב

phrases.notes: It's the best way to do it, but the punishment doesn't depend on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה about a betrothed נערה's punishment. It moves from her convert status to the case where the father's doorway is missing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A betrothed נערה who sinned is stoned even without a father or a father's house. The doorway requirement is only a מצוה.
